dsa5105-erm.title: Train–validation gap lab
dsa5105-erm.learningGoal: Use a held-out validation signal to choose a model complexity instead of celebrating training fit alone.
dsa5105-erm.explanation: The useful choice is near the lowest validation risk, not necessarily the lowest training risk.

dsa5105-linear-week1.title: Linear-model reasoning trace
dsa5105-linear-week1.learningGoal: Move from a hypothesis space to an objective, a closed-form fit, and a regularized extension.
steps: Start by naming the function class and its parameters.
ERM averages the observed losses; it does not directly reveal population risk.
Full column rank is the assumption behind uniqueness.
The penalty stabilizes directions that OLS cannot identify well.
dsa5105-linear-week1.explanation: A formula is easier to remember when the model, loss, assumption, and extension are kept as separate moves.

dsa5105-learning-theory.title: Generalization decision tree
dsa5105-learning-theory.learningGoal: Choose the next evaluation move when training fit and held-out evidence disagree.

splits.label: Training error is lowest
splits.detail: Do not stop: this can be sample-specific fit.

splits.label: Validation risk is lowest
splits.detail: Use validation for model selection, then reserve test for the final estimate.

splits.label: Test score is convenient
splits.detail: Repeated test inspection leaks information into selection.

dsa5105-learning-theory.explanation: The right branch is defined by the evaluation protocol, not by whichever score is easiest to optimize.

dsa5105-linear-regularization.title: Regularization trade-off explorer
dsa5105-linear-regularization.learningGoal: Compare fit and complexity as a penalty changes the model's bias–variance trade-off.
dsa5105-linear-regularization.explanation: A useful penalty is selected by held-out evidence: stronger regularization can reduce variance while increasing bias.

dsa5105-svm-margin.title: Margin and support-vector lab
dsa5105-svm-margin.learningGoal: See how a wider margin can improve geometric robustness while still respecting classification errors.
dsa5105-svm-margin.explanation: Support vectors anchor the boundary; changing the margin changes the trade-off between fit and robustness.

dsa5105-kernel-pca-cluster.title: Unsupervised-method concept map
dsa5105-kernel-pca-cluster.learningGoal: Choose among kernel geometry, PCA compression, K-means grouping, and GMM uncertainty by the question being asked.

nodes.label: K-means
nodes.detail: Assign each point to one nearest centroid.

dsa5105-kernel-pca-cluster.explanation: The map is a method-selection exercise: output and objective matter more than memorizing algorithm names.

dsa5105-pca-deep-dive.title: PCA projection stepper
dsa5105-pca-deep-dive.learningGoal: Trace centering, covariance structure, and projection as three separate reasoning steps.
dsa5105-pca-deep-dive.explanation: PCA is a sequence: remove the mean, find high-variance directions, then represent data in that basis.

dsa5105-cluster-gmm.title: GMM / EM trace
dsa5105-cluster-gmm.learningGoal: Follow how soft assignments and parameter updates alternate until the likelihood stabilizes.
dsa5105-cluster-gmm.explanation: EM alternates an expectation step with a maximization step; each update is conditional on the other.

dsa5105-weighted-ols.title: Weighted OLS derivation trace
dsa5105-weighted-ols.learningGoal: Make the rank assumption and row-weighting transformation explicit before using a closed form.
steps: A nonlinear basis can still be linear in the unknown weights.
Stationarity gives the equation; uniqueness needs full column rank.
Positive example weights change the geometry of the residual.
w_A=(Phi^T A Phi)^-1 Phi^T A y
The inverse is valid only when the weighted normal matrix is nonsingular.
dsa5105-weighted-ols.explanation: The same derivation makes it harder to confuse a formula with the assumptions that justify it.

dsa5105-svm-dual-kkt.title: SVM KKT-to-dual trace
dsa5105-svm-dual-kkt.learningGoal: Follow the path from the margin constraints to alpha balance and support vectors.
steps: Normalize the separator so the closest feasible points define the margin.
The weight vector becomes a combination of training examples.
Positive and negative multiplier mass must balance.
Non-zero multipliers identify active margin constraints: the support vectors.
dsa5105-svm-dual-kkt.explanation: Each step has a different role: geometry, stationarity, feasibility, and active constraints.

dsa5105-trees-ensembles.title: Tree and ensemble reasoning trace
dsa5105-trees-ensembles.learningGoal: Separate a local tree split from the statistical reason an ensemble can generalize better.
steps: Compare weighted child impurity with the parent.
Depth controls the number of regions and can overfit.
Averaging partially uncorrelated errors mainly reduces variance.
AdaBoost gives more influence to a weak learner that is better than random and reweights its mistakes.
dsa5105-trees-ensembles.explanation: The visual sequence keeps impurity, capacity, variance, and sequential reweighting distinct.

dsa5105-neural-backprop.title: Backpropagation computation graph
dsa5105-neural-backprop.learningGoal: Walk a scalar computation graph in reverse and see where each local derivative enters.
steps: Store the intermediate values before differentiating.
Multiply the upstream signal by the sigmoid local derivative.
The final local factors give the parameter gradient; this is efficient, not a global-optimum proof.
dsa5105-neural-backprop.explanation: Backprop is a reusable chain-rule procedure over a graph, not a promise about where non-convex optimization ends.

dsa5105-pca-numerical.title: PCA numerical pipeline
dsa5105-pca-numerical.learningGoal: Keep centering, eigenvectors, reconstruction, and whitening as separate operations.
steps: Remove the feature-wise mean before measuring variation.
The symmetric covariance matrix contains the directional variance.
The top eigenvector maximizes projected variance.
Whitening rescales principal coordinates and can amplify tiny-eigenvalue noise.
dsa5105-pca-numerical.explanation: A correct PCA answer names the data transform, the optimization target, and the reconstruction convention.

dsa5105-gmm-em-numerical.title: GMM responsibility and EM trace
dsa5105-gmm-em-numerical.learningGoal: See the prior-weighted likelihood become a soft assignment and then a parameter update.
steps: Combine how common the component is with how likely it makes the point.
Responsibilities form a probability distribution over components.
Use responsibilities as soft weights in the M-step.
Alternate until the likelihood change is small; initialization can affect the local optimum.
dsa5105-gmm-em-numerical.explanation: The trace makes the difference between hard distance assignment and soft probabilistic responsibility visible.

dsa5105-mdp-value-iteration.title: Value-iteration sweep trace
dsa5105-mdp-value-iteration.learningGoal: Show how a future state's value propagates backward through successive Bellman backups.
steps: State the starting estimate so every sweep is auditable.
Compute one action's expected immediate plus continuation value.
Choose the best action after comparing candidates.
After convergence, convert the value fixed point into a greedy policy.
dsa5105-mdp-value-iteration.explanation: The sequence separates initialization, action evaluation, maximization, and policy extraction.

dsa5105-dynamic-programming.title: Dynamic-programming table trace
dsa5105-dynamic-programming.learningGoal: Derive a recurrence from the final move and make its evaluation order and complexity explicit.
steps: Define what one table entry means before writing algebra.
The recurrence cannot be evaluated without base cases.
time O(n), space O(n) or O(1)
Each state is computed once; rolling storage is possible when only two predecessors are needed.
dsa5105-dynamic-programming.explanation: Dynamic programming is a proof pattern: state meaning, boundary, final-choice decomposition, and complexity.

dsa5105-graph-kernel-pagerank.title: Graph-kernel and PageRank trace
dsa5105-graph-kernel-pagerank.learningGoal: Connect PSD reasoning by Gram matrices with fixed-point reasoning by power iteration.
steps: An inner product representation gives a PSD Gram matrix.
P is stochastic; repair dangling nodes
PageRank needs a probability-preserving transition operator.
Damping and repeated multiplication approach the stationary ranking.
dsa5105-graph-kernel-pagerank.explanation: The lab makes two exam proof patterns concrete: non-negative Gram quadratic forms and normalized fixed-point iteration.

dsa5105-spectral-clustering.title: Spectral-clustering pipeline
dsa5105-spectral-clustering.learningGoal: Follow adjacency, degree, Laplacian energy, eigenvectors, and final K-means assignment.
steps: Convert edge weights into node degrees.
The matrix penalizes disagreement across connected nodes.
Low-energy non-constant eigenvectors describe smooth graph partitions.
Use the spectral embedding for a final assignment step.
dsa5105-spectral-clustering.explanation: Spectral clustering is a pipeline, not a single magic eigenvector: graph, operator, embedding, assignment.

dsa5105-ls-svm-loo.title: LS-SVM and LOO trace
dsa5105-ls-svm-loo.learningGoal: Compare ridge, LS-SVM KKT blocks, and leverage-corrected leave-one-out residuals.
steps: LS-SVM equality constraints produce a block linear system.
The diagonal H_ii measures self-influence or leverage.
Correct the in-sample residual without refitting N separate models.
dsa5105-ls-svm-loo.explanation: The same regularized-linear-algebra theme appears in three exam formats: normal equations, KKT blocks, and LOO shortcuts.

dsa5105-rl-gnn.title: RL and GNN information-flow map
dsa5105-rl-gnn.learningGoal: Distinguish value propagation over transitions from representation propagation over graph neighbors.

nodes.label: Bellman
nodes.detail: Back up reward plus discounted continuation value.

nodes.label: Update
nodes.detail: Mix the aggregate with the node state.

dsa5105-rl-gnn.explanation: Both systems move information locally, but RL follows possible transitions while a GNN follows observed edges.

dsa5105-rl-bellman.title: Bellman backup timeline
dsa5105-rl-bellman.learningGoal: Separate immediate reward from discounted continuation value in one decision step.
dsa5105-rl-bellman.explanation: A Bellman backup turns a long return into local evidence plus a discounted estimate of what follows.

dsa5105-gnn.title: GNN message-passing builder
dsa5105-gnn.learningGoal: Build one permutation-invariant graph layer from neighbor messages, aggregation, and node update.
dsa5105-gnn.explanation: The graph layer is a pipeline: transform neighbors, aggregate the set, then combine with the node state.
